title: Component communication: input, output and content projection

videos.script:
Components have to talk to each other. Today you learn the three ways, and the planner gets its second screen. {{inputs}} An input is data handed down from a parent. The week loads the data once and passes the summary its two numbers. The summary stops knowing where they came from, and the second request for the file disappears.

{{page}} Then the course page, given its course by an input. In lesson 17 the router will set that same input from the address.

{{outputs}} An output is news passed up. A row says it was ticked, and the page that owns the data decides what to do. You tick a session, and the page updates. And the week above it does not. Two copies of the data disagree on one screen, which is what lesson 6 warned about, and lesson 11 fixes.

{{model}} Model is a value that goes both ways, for controls. {{projection}} Content projection passes markup into a frame, and the week gets a panel. {{queries}} A query reaches one element, here to move the keyboard's focus.
